sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This 0.5–1.5 m deciduous shrub is endemic to the coastal plain of the Carolinas, United States. It grows in wet, acidic habitats, including pine savannas and swamp margins.

sections.title: Leaves and flowering
sections.text: The alternate leaves are about 2–6 cm long and 0.5–3 cm wide. Cream flowers, often marked by an internal red band, are approximately 12–14 × 13–20 mm and occur in clusters of 3–10; they produce a capsule.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: The sources consulted do not establish a food use or a species-specific toxicological risk. As a precaution, do not eat this plant.
